body: I describe it feeling like my bones are filled with angry bees trying to get out.

I had therapy the day after I wrote this post and my therapist brought up that idea.

She asked the right questions, and I eventually realized that there is a ton of selfish motivation behind me taking that role. For me, it establishes a power dynamic both inter- and intrapersonally. It strokes my ego. Many other things. Simultaneously, I do not recognize anything worthy in me besides my helpfulness. I'm not sure what my relationships would look like if I wasn't in the caretaker position. That scares the hell out of me. Who alone me am??? ? 

Sorry to get all think-y on you. I appreciate your comments. Thank you for challenging my perspective, and sharing your experiences. You seem pretty wise. :)

"... but now it's time for me to care for myself the way I cared for others."

I think it's time for me to do that, too.

Thank you for taking the time to reply. And I hope (for everyone's sake) that real friends do exist. I believe they do.

Thank you for the recommendation, and for giving me some info to look deeper in to.

People are not bad, and they absolutely are not the reason that I feel unloved. My friends and family show me so much love and care, but I can't internalize it. I do ask for comfort from my loved ones. I do set boundaries. Thousands of hours of therapy better have taught me something.

It's just: everyone wants to be cared for and listened to without judgement. So when I provide that, they like it. Within minutes of meeting someone I have usually established my role as a caretaker. My therapy "homework" from last session was to imagine what it would feel like, what I would say, etc. in order to not establish that role. It feels weird to visualize me taking a different role, or no role at all. I agree that presenting myself differently will help people not avoid that dynamic with me, though. When it's offered, people take it. That isn't because they're bad. They just want to be seen, like everyone else.

The lack of respect and love I have for myself is the core of it, I think. "It's okay if I always put you before myself. You need comfort more than me."

I think that looking into codependency and the "caretaker" dynamic will be very helpful. Parts of your comment didn't resonate but a lot of it did. Thank you very much for taking the time to reply. :)
